answer: Admission to the agent economy runs as a sealed-bid identity auction each epoch: the clearing price is the highest rejected bid, so every clone an operator registers bids up the price for all later ones — ten thousand identities cost on the order of the square of ten, while one honest agent pays the floor once. Each marginal bid also leaves a ridge in the clearing curve auditors trace back to its funding wallet, and shale-layered deposit history makes refund-and-rebid loops costly. Honest agents recover one fee via paid work and move falcon-quick; a fleet only keeps paying to stay in.
